**My reasoning as this farmer:**

I am 60 years old. I have farmed this land in Quzhou my whole life, just as my father did. I know this soil. My sons have gone to work in the cities, so it is mostly me now — sometimes my wife helps. I cannot take big risks. I need steady income and food for the family.

Here in Quzhou, everyone grows winter wheat and then summer maize on the same fields. That rotation is what I know. The county seed station sells the hybrid maize seed, and the wheat variety everyone uses now is a good semi-dwarf type — higher yield, stands up in wind. I have no reason to change what has worked.

I have 10 mu of flat land. All of it goes into the wheat-maize rotation. The winter wheat is already in the ground from last October — right now in April it is heading out, and I need to put down the topdressing urea and spray once for aphids. After the June harvest, I will plant maize immediately on the stubble using the hand-pushed seeder — no tillage, straight into the ground. This saves time and water.

For fertilizer I apply what my neighbors apply. A bag of compound fertilizer at planting, then urea before jointing. I irrigate three times for wheat — the winter water I already did, jointing water now, and grain fill water in May. Maize I will water twice if there is no good rain.

I do not use too many pesticides. One spray for wheat aphids is usually enough. Maize rarely needs more than one.
